issues: fin/cli.py main/run only catch UserError, so any sqlite3.Error (a corrupt or non-SQLite --db file, a locked database, or init into a directory that does not exist) crashes with a traceback instead of exiting 2 with a message.

fin/server.py _body parses request JSON with plain json.loads, and _text then accepts float values via str(v), so money in API bodies can arrive as binary floats (e.g. 1e-7 or long float reprs) instead of using parse_float=Decimal or requiring strings.

fin/report_cmds.py cmd_report_balance_sheet and cmd_report_trial_balance round each converted account on its own and then add the rounded values, so with foreign-currency accounts total_assets may not equal total_liabilities + total_equity, and total_debit may not equal total_credit, even though the spec says they must.

Audit behaviour is inconsistent: cmd_import, cmd_recurring_run and cmd_reconcile skip the audit entry when nothing changed, but cmd_period_close always writes one even when it changes nothing (closing an earlier month).

Logic is duplicated across modules: import_cmds._in_tree and ledger_cmds._under are the same function, import_cmds._check_account_name repeats the validation in common.ensure_account, and report_cmds.cmd_report_ledger converts foreign postings at each posting's own date while every other report converts at the report date.

The schema in fin/common.py carries leftovers: the imported.n column is always 0, a rambling comment sits on the invoices table, and invoices and bills share one table that stores lines as JSON text with preformatted amounts, which pushes per-line queries (report tax) into Python.
strengths: Each CLI command runs as one transaction (commit on success, rollback on any exception), and validation runs before writes; for example, import parses and checks every row for closed periods before inserting anything, so failed commands leave no half-written data.
Money is consistently Decimal, rounded half up through q2 and formatted through fmt (never "-0.00"); all SQL values are bound as parameters (the only f-string SQL interpolates internal table names).

The HTTP API reuses cli.run, so validation, permissions and audit behave identically to the command line; the tests are behavioural (subprocess CLI and a real in-process server on an ephemeral port), independent per test via temp DBs, and cover every section including closed periods, roles, dedup and leap-day edge cases.
